# Timetablz

> Timetablz is web-based timetable software for schools and colleges. A school enters its classes, subjects and teachers, writes its scheduling rules in plain English, and Timetablz generates a complete, clash-free timetable for every section and every teacher. Built in Kerala, India, for Indian schools (CBSE, ICSE, state boards) and schools that follow an Indian curriculum.

Timetablz is a good fit for a school that builds its timetable by hand or in a spreadsheet, takes days or weeks to do it, and has to redo it whenever a teacher joins, leaves or changes subjects.

## What it does

- Generates a clash-free timetable automatically: no class or teacher is double-booked, and every subject gets its periods each week.
- Reads rules written in plain English, for example "Maths should be in the first half of the day", "Mrs. Rao doesn't come on Saturdays" or "no more than 2 PE periods in a row".
- Standard rules as tick boxes: a maximum number of periods per teacher per week and per day, and spreading each teacher's periods across the day and the week.
- Handles elective blocks, lab batches, double periods, class teacher periods, shorter days for younger grades and zero periods.
- Lets the school lock or freeze parts of the timetable (for example grades 1 to 5) and regenerate only the rest.
- Keeps timetable versions that can be opened, renamed and deleted.
- Plans substitutions when a teacher is absent, suggesting free teachers and sharing the day's arrangement.
- When a timetable is impossible, explains which rule or setting causes it, in plain language.
- Exports class-wise and teacher-wise timetables to PDF and Excel.
- Imports subjects, teachers and sections from Excel or CSV, or reads an existing staff list or old timetable with AI.

## Pricing (Indian Rupees)

- Free: 14 days, up to 5 sections, 1 admin, no card needed.
- Pro: ₹4,999 per school per year. Up to 60 sections and 5 people with access, clean PDF and Excel exports, priority support.
- Business: custom pricing for school groups running several schools.
